messages.text: The morning light filtered through the classroom windows, casting long rectangles of gold across the polished wooden desks. I stood at the doorway, my fingers wrapped around the strap of my bag so tightly that my knuckles had gone white. The classroom buzzed with the indistinct murmur of conversations — the kind of ambient noise that fills every high school homeroom five minutes before the bell. Except today, it was different. Today, they were all talking about me. I felt an invisible weight pressing down on my shoulders, as if the entire room was judging me before I'd even said a word.

Sensei Tanaka adjusted his glasses with a precise, almost mechanical motion. He gestured toward me with an open palm, and the invisible wall between the corridor and the classroom vanished. I stepped forward, my footsteps echoing loudly in the sudden silence.

messages.name: Kazuhiko
messages.text: My name is Kazuhiko. I just moved here from Osaka. Please take care of me.

I bowed, then Sensei Tanaka pointed to an empty desk near the window. "You can sit there, next to Anna." The girl with dark waves raised her hand in a lazy wave. I walked toward the seat, the silence feeling awkward, punctuated only by the creak of the floorboards.

messages.name: Anna
messages.text: Hey, new guy. You looked like a deer caught in headlights up there. Don't worry, it gets easier.

I didn't know what to say to that, so I just nodded. The lesson began, but my mind drifted. I thought of the river bank near my old school in Osaka, where I used to walk alone after class. Now everything felt different. At least I had a bit of money in the bank from my part-time job back home, so I could buy lunch without worrying. But fitting in? That was a different kind of currency.
